Title: The Sage's Secret

FADE IN:

EXT. MAIN STREET - MORNING

A quaint small town comes alive as people go about their daily routines. A gentle breeze carries the scent of fresh-baked bread.

INT. BAKERY - MORNING

MRS. JOHNSON (50s, warm, and welcoming) serves a CUSTOMER behind the counter.

CUSTOMER: (smiling) Another beautiful morning in Maple Falls, isn't it?

MRS. JOHNSON: (smiling back) It is indeed.

The bell above the door chimes as RACHEL (mid-30s, determined, and slightly troubled) enters.

MRS. JOHNSON: Rachel, good to see you. What can I get you today?

RACHEL: Just a coffee, please.

As Rachel waits for her coffee, she notices a flyer on the bulletin board. It's an invitation to a job fair at the local college.

INT. RACHEL'S APARTMENT - LATER

Rachel sits at her kitchen table, sipping her coffee, and staring at the flyer. She looks up as a knock comes at the door.

RACHEL: (calling out) Come in.

MRS. KING (late 40s, kind-hearted, and wise) enters, carrying a basket of freshly baked goods.

MRS. KING: Rachel, I heard you were out of work. I thought I'd bring you some treats to brighten your day.

RACHEL: (grateful) That's very kind of you, Mrs. King. I appreciate it.

They share a warm moment before Mrs. King notices the flyer.

MRS. KING: Ah, a job fair, eh? I think I might have just the thing for you.

INT. LIBRARY - DAY

Rachel and Mrs. King sit in the quiet library, surrounded by shelves of books. Mrs. King tells Rachel about an old sage who lives on the outskirts of town. He's known for his wisdom and has a hidden talent for helping people find their true calling.

RACHEL: (intrigued) A sage? Really?

MRS. KING: (smiling) Indeed. He's a bit reclusive and doesn't see many visitors, but he has a special gift. I think he could help you, Rachel.

INT. SAGE'S HUT - AFTERNOON

Rachel approaches the sage's hut, feeling a sense of unease. The old man, SAGE (70s, mysterious, and insightful), greets her warmly.

SAGE: Ah, Rachel. Welcome to my humble abode. Please, have a seat.

They sit down across from each other, and Rachel begins to explain her situation.

RACHEL: I've been out of work for a while now. I've tried everything I can think of, but nothing seems to be working out. I just don't know what I'm supposed to be doing.

SAGE: (leaning forward) Sometimes, my dear, we must look within ourselves to find the answers we seek. I sense that you have a great gift, a unique talent, but it has yet to be revealed to you.

RACHEL: (doubting) I don't know about that. I've never felt particularly special or talented.

SAGE: (smiling) That's where you're wrong, my dear. We all have gifts, and sometimes they take time to surface. But when they do, they can change the world.

INT. COLLEGE CAMPUS - DAY

Months later, Rachel stands proudly on the stage at the college graduation ceremony, receiving her diploma. She looks out at the crowd, grateful for the wisdom of the sage and the kindness of Mrs. King.

RACHEL: (smiling) I never would have found my calling without them.

FADE OUT.

---

THE END.
